title: Setup-script exit 2 ('[x]abort', documented as stop the run) is treated as an ordinary failure: both installers continue with the next step and scripts/aitools reports 'Completed with errors'
observation: interactive-menus.md:74 and :88 say only `abort` is global ('stop the run'); aitools-lib.sh:915 and :1075 ('Exits with code 2 on abort'); reference/managed-file-deployment.md:44 and :54 ('[x]abort --> exit 2'). aitools-install.sh validate_and_run (:154-173) logs any non-zero exit as '<name> failed (exit N)' with write_summary ERROR and returns, and the installer goes on to the next step (call sites such as :291, :609, :721); aitools-install.ps1 Invoke-ValidatedScript (:92-119) does the same. scripts/aitools:1604-1616 maps any installer non-zero to 'Completed with errors' and overall_rc=1; aitools.ps1:1495-1509 does the same ($installerRc non-zero -> 'Completed with errors', $overallRc = 1).
expected: .claude/rules/interactive-menus.md 'JSON field-level review' (abort is global, stops the run); reference/managed-file-deployment.md state machine ([x]abort --> exit 2).
impact: A user who chooses [x]abort in a managed-file or JSON field review still gets every later installer step run against their machine, and the run is reported as an error rather than an abort.
discoveryContext: Found by mission S5-Tools (I-02, I-24; reviewer S5-Tools-A D-07) (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-20/21) and consolidated by S4-Review, which de-duplicated it against incidents #1-#86 (origin/main 26c37b2 registries/incidents.json). Audited: interactive-menus.md, aitools-lib.sh prompt_diff_review, aitools-install.sh validate_and_run, aitools-install.ps1 Invoke-ValidatedScript, scripts/aitools installer_rc handling. Citations re-verified by S3-Ledger (mission LEDGER, session 10cf255a-c) against origin/main c8573ed on 2026-10-21; file:line references added. Bash and PS1 together. (Draft plan reference at filing, not an approved tracker: M2 batches B4a/B4b (S5-Tools plan).)

title: A merge the user accepts without adopting (Merge-Conflict [m]erge, or Auto-Merge [a]ccept with no adopt label) is silently reverted to the unchanged source by the next run's auto-deploy

expected: reference/managed-file-deployment.md 'State Machine' and 'Menus': [m]erge is an 'AI-assisted merge of source + local' that is deployed ('updated'); nothing in the spec says the merged content is discarded on the next run. Commander-approved managed-file model (2026-10-21, mission packet section 6; text on branch docs/managed-file-choices, not yet merged): SOURCE is the source of truth, no ancestor and no deploy state, and adopt and merge are copied to the repo immediately by the library.

discoveryContext: Verified 2026-10-21 by Session Commander 10cf255a-c with .scratch/session-10cf255a-c/merge-revert-test.sh (isolated HOME; output in merge-revert-home/logs/deploy.log); handed to S3-Incidents for filing. title: check-pre-push.sh step 3 secret pattern uses `[\s]` inside an ERE bracket expression, so it flags words like 'tokens:' and misses 'token = value'; the PS1 twin uses a real \s
observation: scripts/check-pre-push.sh:68 (origin/main db4b3c5): secret_pattern='(password|secret|api_key|api-key|apikey|token|bearer|private_key|AWS_ACCESS|ANTHROPIC_API)[\s]*[=:]', used with `grep -iE` at :69. In a POSIX ERE bracket expression `[\s]` is the two characters backslash and 's'. S3-Incidents probe with macOS /usr/bin/grep (BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD), .scratch/session-S3-Incidents/secret-probe.sh: '+Path tokens: a b' MATCH, '+tokens= y' MATCH, '+token=abc' MATCH, '+token = abc' no-match, '+password : x' no-match. scripts/check-pre-push.ps1:69 uses .NET `\s*[=:]`, which matches the whitespace forms. PR #58's pre-push run failed step 3 on the phrase 'Path tokens:' (S3-Gate).

impact: On macOS and Linux, an added line such as `password = hunter2` or `api_key : ...` passes the secret scan and can be pushed, while harmless prose ('tokens:') fails it, so the check is both noisy and blind in the common spaced form. Windows runs catch the spaced form.
discoveryContext: Found by S3-Gate (mission GATE, PR #58 'Verification': step 3 false positive, `[\s]` analysis); listed by Session Commander 10cf255a-c for this batch (2026-10-21). suggestedResolution: Use `[[:space:]]*` in the bash pattern (portable ERE), add a word boundary after the keyword so plurals in prose do not match (for example `(password|...|token)s?[[:space:]]*[=:][[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]`), and add a seeded test case for both forms on bash and PS1.
